learning_outcomes.text: Apply the acquired knowledge to identify, formulate and solve problems in broad contexts, being able to integrate them by working in multidisciplinary teams.
Communicate knowledge and conclusions, both orally and in writing, to specialized and non-specialized audiences clearly and unambiguously.
Possess learning skills that allow continuous study throughout life for adequate professional development.
Organization and planning of projects and human teams. Teamwork and leadership capacity.
Ability to defend ideas and points of view indicating pros and cons of different options. Attitudes of critical reasoning and creative actions based on open situations.
Knowledge and abilities to understand the main ideas of complex general and specialized texts.
Ability to relate to English speakers with a sufficient degree of fluency and naturalness.
Ability to produce clear and detailed texts on various topics.

syllabus_topics: Presentations
Presentations: Functional competencies: Introducing oneself, greeting, giving information about oneself.
Presentations: Grammar: Present indicative of some verbs, articles, interrogation, possessives.
Presentations: Vocabulary: Professions, company roles, object description, geometric shapes.
Professional contact
Professional contact: Functional competencies: Requesting and offering something, talking about habits and frequency, expressing tastes and desires.
Professional contact: Grammar: Present indicative of some verbs, negation, some pronouns, some prepositions.
Professional contact: Vocabulary: Professional activity sectors, meteorology, family, numbers, dimensions, units of measurement.
Online communication
Online communication: Functional competencies: Communicating by phone and internet, writing emails.
Online communication: Grammar: Present indicative of some verbs, some prepositions, time indicators, expressing cause.
Online communication: Vocabulary: Telephone and computer communication, description of materials and operations.
Professional trips
Professional trips: Functional competencies: Giving instructions, asking for and indicating directions or locations, talking about means of transport and accommodation.
Professional trips: Grammar: Imperative, formation of feminine and plural, impersonal expressions.
Professional trips: Vocabulary: Travel, means of transport, accommodation, location, mathematics.
Organization of the professional day
Organization of the professional day: Functional competencies: Talking about daily activities, giving instructions, making appointments.
Organization of the professional day: Grammar: Pronominal verbs, near future, some prepositions, partitives, demonstratives.
Organization of the professional day: Vocabulary: Professional activities, food, chronology, instructions.
Choosing
Choosing: Functional competencies: Choosing and ordering in commercial establishments, indicating and asking for prices, talking about past events.
Choosing: Grammar: Direct personal pronouns, comparatives, "passé composé", temporal indicators of the past.
Choosing: Vocabulary: Restaurants, sales, rentals, accommodation, shopping, clothing, function of machines and tools.
Company presentation

Company presentation: Functional competencies: Talking about a company and its organization, describing manufacturing processes, describing personal and professional qualities, indicating product composition, expressing obligation and prohibition.
Company presentation: Grammar: Relatives, some personal pronouns.
Company presentation: Vocabulary: Companies and their organization, processes, laboratory experiments.
Job search
Job search: Functional competencies: Understanding and drafting a job offer, writing a curriculum vitae, conducting a job interview.
Job search: Grammar: Recent past, time expressions, imperfect past.
Job search: Vocabulary: Job offers, curriculum vitae, function of machines and tools.
assessment_rules: To pass the course, students must obtain a minimum grade of 50% in all evaluations and tests. In the Ordinary Call, there are two evaluation paths: Progressive Evaluation or Global Evaluation. Progressive Evaluation requires a minimum grade of 50% in each of its components: Oral and written comprehension exams (50%), Oral expression exam (25%), and Written expression exam (25%). Global Evaluation (Ordinary Call) and the Extraordinary Call both consist of a single final exam that evaluates all French language skills (oral comprehension, written comprehension, oral expression, and written expression), where students must obtain a minimum grade of 50%.
